name: Hakone: Secret Box Puzzles
subtitle: Slide, press, tilt, open
shortDescription: Thirty-five Japanese trick boxes with real moving parts: sliding panels, rolling bolts, hidden catches and a daily box.
longDescription:
The himitsu-bako, or hidden box, comes from the Hakone region of Japan, where craftsmen fitted marquetry boxes with hidden sliding panels that open only in the right order. Hakone: hidden Box Puzzles is a collection of trick boxes with real moving parts, made to be opened slowly.

Drag panels along their grooves, press hidden catches and tilt the whole box so brass bolts roll downhill. Every part frees or holds another. If a panel stops against the wood, work out why and open the lid. It is real 3D, with yosegi marquetry in cedar, walnut, red lacquer, mulberry and ebony, lit like a tea-room tabletop.

Five bench lessons teach one idea at a time. Hint glows the next part, and Think says in plain words what to do and why. In Auto Play the computer opens the box while you watch, with Pause, speed, Think and Take over at any moment.

Collect 35 boxes in five collections, from gentle catches to long, careful openings. A new Daily Box arrives every day, the same for everyone, with a streak. A shelf of keepsakes waits inside: a tea bowl, a spinning top, a little bell, a jade bead and more. Earn stars for fewest moves, see statistics and twelve achievements.

Calm by design: three room lights, text zoom up to 300 percent on every reading page, and portrait and landscape layouts. It works offline with no account.

Free with ads. Go ad-free with a monthly pass or earn ad-free time from videos.
monetization: Free with ads, optional monthly ad-free
